CWE-22.name: Path Traversal
CWE-22.explanation: An attacker can trick the app into reading or writing files outside the intended folder — for example, reaching system files.

CWE-77.name: Command Injection
CWE-77.explanation: Unsanitized input is passed to a system shell, letting an attacker run their own commands on the server.

CWE-78.name: OS Command Injection
CWE-78.explanation: Attacker-controlled input reaches the operating system's command interpreter, allowing arbitrary commands.

CWE-79.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.explanation: An attacker can slip malicious JavaScript into a web page, running in other users' browsers and stealing their sessions.

CWE-89.name: SQL Injection
CWE-89.explanation: Unsanitized input goes into a database query, letting an attacker read, modify, or delete data they shouldn't.

CWE-94.name: Code Injection
CWE-94.explanation: The app executes attacker-supplied code — often the most severe category because it gives direct control.

CWE-119.name: Buffer Overflow
CWE-119.explanation: The app writes more data into memory than it should, letting an attacker overwrite nearby data or crash it.

CWE-125.name: Out-of-Bounds Read
CWE-125.explanation: The app reads memory it shouldn't, often leaking passwords or keys held nearby.

CWE-200.name: Information Disclosure
CWE-200.explanation: The app leaks data it shouldn't — passwords, keys, file paths, or internal configuration.

CWE-287.name: Improper Authentication
CWE-287.explanation: The system can be tricked into letting an attacker in without the correct credentials.

CWE-306.name: Missing Authentication
CWE-306.explanation: A critical function can be reached without authentication at all — no login required.

CWE-311.name: Missing Encryption
CWE-311.explanation: Sensitive data is stored or transmitted without encryption, exposing it to anyone listening or reading storage.

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.explanation: A malicious site can make a logged-in user's browser perform actions they didn't intend.

CWE-400.name: Resource Exhaustion
CWE-400.explanation: An attacker consumes CPU, memory, or disk until the service becomes unavailable (DoS).

CWE-416.name: Use-After-Free
CWE-416.explanation: The app uses memory after freeing it, letting an attacker redirect execution — often to run their own code.

CWE-434.name: Unrestricted File Upload
CWE-434.explanation: Attacker can upload files that the server later executes — often leading to full compromise.

CWE-476.name: Null Pointer Dereference
CWE-476.explanation: The app accesses null memory, usually crashing — typically a denial-of-service.

CWE-502.name: Unsafe Deserialization
CWE-502.explanation: Untrusted data is converted back into objects, letting an attacker inject code or manipulate the app's state.

CWE-611.name: XML External Entity (XXE)
CWE-611.explanation: The app parses XML that references external entities, letting attackers read files or reach internal services.

CWE-787.name: Out-of-Bounds Write
CWE-787.explanation: The app writes past the end of allocated memory, letting an attacker corrupt data or run their own code.

CWE-798.name: Hardcoded Credentials
CWE-798.explanation: Passwords or keys are baked into the code — anyone who reads the binary or repo has them.

CWE-829.name: Supply Chain — Untrusted Include
CWE-829.explanation: The app includes code from a source an attacker controls, such as a compromised third-party library.

CWE-862.name: Missing Authorization
CWE-862.explanation: The app doesn't check whether the user is *allowed* to do the action, so a regular user can trigger admin actions.

CWE-863.name: Incorrect Authorization
CWE-863.explanation: The permission check exists but has a flaw, letting an attacker escalate privileges.

CWE-918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
CWE-918.explanation: Attacker can make your server send requests to internal systems — bypassing firewalls.

CWE-1321.name: Prototype Pollution
CWE-1321.explanation: An attacker injects properties into JavaScript objects that every other object inherits, often leading to code execution.
